A marine biologist randomly samples starfish from two different rockpools. The lengths, in centimeters, of starfish from the first and second rockpools are denoted $x_{i}$ and $y_{i}$, respectively, where the sizes of each sample are $n_{1} = 15$ and $n_{2} = 20$. The results are summarized below.

$∑_(i = 1)^(15)x_{i} = 144, ∑_(i = 1)^(15)x_{i}^{2} = 1416, ∑_(i = 1)^(20)y_{i} = 194, ∑_(i = 1)^(20)y_{i}^{2} = 1918$

Given that the samples from each rockpool are independent and the population variance $σ^{2}$ in each rockpool may be assumed to be the same, find a pooled estimate for $σ^{2}$, rounded to one decimal place.

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.

:knowledge-point/title: Finding a Pooled Estimate of Variance for Two Samples of Different Size
